purpose: Record representative comparable mountainboard/e-MTB architectures and the specific mechanical lessons used by X1. These are design references, not authority over received X1 hardware.

references.x1_lesson: Use this as the first physical rolling-chassis reference. Preserve stock 8-inch interfaces until measured evidence justifies a change.

observed_architecture: 70 mm axle upgrade creates an ultra-wide 440 mm drivetrain-compatible variant
references.x1_lesson: Brake compatibility is proven only for the brake-first family. A 70 mm axle conversion changes axial geometry and must be re-qualified before assuming the V5 still aligns.
Do not merge the 420 mm drive geometry and 400 mm brake geometry into one fictional truck. They are separate reference branches until a topology test selects one.

observed_architecture: manual calls for brake inspection before riding
references.x1_lesson: Treat rear-wheel placement, rotor/hub stack, arm sweep, cable sweep, pad rebound and service inspection as real constraints. Brake qualification never authorizes traction power.

observed_architecture: 44 mm diagonal common four-hole motor pattern
wheel couplers, motor gears, motors and guards are separate interface items
references.x1_lesson: Gear-drive strength does not solve interface coexistence. Model coupler, skid, guard, motor, wheel-removal and axial-space envelopes explicitly.

Production off-road architecture favors strong wide drive trucks, guarded gears, top-side battery protection and serviceable couplers. It does not establish simultaneous V5 mechanical-brake compatibility.

Matrix III plus dual gear drive and 8-inch pneumatics is a proven high-power packaging family. X1 should remain lighter/lower-power where mission requirements permit rather than copying peak specification.

observed_architecture: buggy-like independent suspension instead of skate trucks
motors kept as sprung mass rather than hub motors
G4 rear belt drive and G4X all-wheel belt drive family
approximately 20 kg G4 and 25 kg G4X complete mass
references.x1_lesson: Independent suspension is a valid solution when speed/terrain demand it, but it multiplies joints, mass and cost. Do not adopt it for X1 unless donor testing demonstrates a specific terrain-control deficiency that truck tuning and pneumatic tires cannot solve.

observed_architecture: DIY mechanical chassis sold separately from electronics
belt drivetrain and motor mounting plates
mechanical chassis alone priced around 1880 USD in the dated review
references.x1_lesson: A mature independent-suspension chassis costs nearly the low-end target for the entire X1 build before electronics. This is strong evidence to preserve the simpler donor architecture unless its physical limits are actually reached.

observed_architecture: roughly 22 kg belt-drive and 24 kg gear-drive complete masses
independent wheel contact prioritized for rough-surface stability
references.x1_lesson: Eight-inch pneumatics remain viable even with independent suspension. Suspension should be justified by measured contact/stability need, not assumed necessary merely because X1 is off-road.

High-speed stability and drive alignment can be improved inside a conventional truck architecture through bearing support, retention, damping/tuning and dedicated motor-mount geometry. Complexity should be added locally before replacing the whole chassis concept.

observed_architecture: front braking selected for forward weight transfer
references.x1_lesson: Front friction braking is a proven mountainboard topology when designed around a dedicated brake truck. This is an existence proof, not permission to improvise a brake adapter onto Matrix III.

observed_architecture: final gear backlash must be set only after truck, wheels and drive are assembled
service knowledge is treated as part of ownership
references.x1_lesson: A drivetrain has assembly-state variables that CAD cannot freeze. Backlash/tension, guard clearance and maintenance checks must become commissioning evidence.

observed_architecture: spare belt and inner tube recommended for rides
references.x1_lesson: Belt drive remains a credible fallback if it uniquely solves brake packaging, but its debris, tension, idler, spare-belt and guard failure modes must be accepted explicitly.
Design inspection and positive-retention features around common mundane failures rather than assuming nominal CAD alignment survives trail vibration.

observed_architecture: insufficient threadlocker/retention preceded wheel loss and axle-thread damage
references.x1_lesson: Wheel retention requires a defined fastener stack, torque/retention procedure, witness marks and pre/post-ride inspection rather than an informal tighten-and-forget step.

observed_architecture: successful long ride with enclosure mounting identified as the outstanding mechanical problem
references.x1_lesson: Battery/enclosure mounting is a primary structural load path. It needs isolation, positive retention, service access and fatigue inspection, not just a waterproof box.
